commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-55973: Require distinct repeated Questionnaire answers
commits.summary: Updated active Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse source so repeated question answers must be distinct.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-55973 explicitly decided that repeated Questionnaire answers must be distinct and that QuestionnaireResponse should carry an invariant prohibiting duplicate answers for the same question. The changed Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse StructureDefinition sources are active conformance inputs, so the commit aligns current rendered/conformance content with that decision.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55973 was Applied/Persuasive and resolved to add a QuestionnaireResponse.item invariant stating that the same answer cannot be specified more than once for the same question, and to update Questionnaire.item.repeats definition/comment text from multiple answers to multiple distinct answers while moving the group/question representation note to the start of the comment. Before this commit, the active Questionnaire source still allowed the older non-distinct wording and the active QuestionnaireResponse source lacked the qrs-4 invariant. Updating those StructureDefinition XML files is required because they are the authoritative source for the current resource definitions and generated conformance artifacts.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are authoritative StructureDefinition inputs for Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse. The Questionnaire edit changes reader-visible element definition/comment text, and the QuestionnaireResponse edit adds a validation invariant and condition reference that affect generated conformance resources and validation behavior for repeated answers.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as the Jira-backed fix for FHIR-55973; no alternate attribution or new WG path is needed for these source changes.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Jira resolution specifically required adding a QuestionnaireResponse.item invariant with human text prohibiting the same answer more than once for the same question, changing Questionnaire.item.repeats definition/comment wording to say multiple distinct answers, and moving the group/question representation wording to the first paragraph. The commit implements those same requirements in the active StructureDefinition sources.

caveats: The expression is implemented as answer.value.isDistinct().allTrue(), which is consistent with enforcing distinct answer values at QuestionnaireResponse.item context.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-56201: Align lastVersionPresent CRMI reference
commits.summary: Updated the FHIR-core lastVersionPresent concept property definition and narrative table to reference the final CRMI includeNoLongerPresent parameter name.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: the core concept property text was left pointing at an obsolete CRMI ValueSet/$expand parameter name. The specific rename is better attributed to FHIR-55634, with FHIR-56201 providing the linked core concept-property context.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-56201 resolved that the core Concept Properties code system should define lastVersionPresent and include it in the defined concept-properties table, but its text still reflected the earlier includeLastVersionPresent name. FHIR-55634, reopened because of that core resolution, finally resolved the CRMI ValueSet/$expand parameter as includeNoLongerPresent and states that returned concepts SHOULD carry the lastVersionPresent property. The edited CodeSystem XML and CodeSystem narrative table are active source for the current spec, so the stale cross-reference conflicts with the final linked Jira decision and should be updated to the final parameter name.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The CodeSystem source is an active conformance artifact for http://hl7.org/fhir/concept-properties, and the notes table is reader-visible narrative on the CodeSystem page. Leaving includeLastVersionPresent in those surfaces would publish an incorrect cross-reference for implementers looking for the CRMI parameter that controls use of lastVersionPresent.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as a Jira-backed correction, but cite FHIR-55634 alongside FHIR-56201 because FHIR-55634 is the decision that finalizes includeNoLongerPresent.

jira_evidence.explanation: This Applied/Persuasive with Modification core issue required adding lastVersionPresent as a string concept property and adding it to the defined concept-properties table. It explains why the property and its expansion semantics belong in core, but its own resolution used the intermediate includeLastVersionPresent wording.

This linked Applied/Persuasive with Modification CRMI issue resolved the ValueSet/$expand input parameter as includeNoLongerPresent and states that affected expansion concepts SHOULD have the lastVersionPresent concept property. That final CRMI parameter decision directly requires the core cross-reference to use includeNoLongerPresent rather than includeLastVersionPresent.

caveats: The change does not alter the lastVersionPresent code, datatype, or semantics; it only corrects the CRMI parameter name referenced from authoritative and narrative core source.
Confluence references for the 2026-04-06 Vocabulary minutes also record reopening FHIR-55634 to update the input parameter name to includeNoLongerPresent.

triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55483 was resolved persuasive/applied to add ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames as an unsignedInt carrying DICOM Number Of Frames (0028,0008) for multiframe instances. The current StructureDefinition had the new element but still described it with an instance-ordinal short, a malformed DICOM tag spelling, and a definition typo; the ImagingStudy ballot note used the non-existent plural path ImagingStudy.series.instances.numberOfFrames. Correcting those active source surfaces is required to align the rendered element details and narrative with the approved element and its intended meaning.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition is the authoritative conformance source for ImagingStudy element definitions and DICOM mappings, so the stale text and mapping affect rendered definitions and generated conformance artifacts. The introduction text is reader-visible narrative. The SVG diagram is a secondary rendered surface; its omission of the added element matters only as diagram consistency alongside the authoritative source update.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the StructureDefinition and narrative corrections as the FHIR-55483 application fix. If resource diagrams are normally regenerated rather than hand-maintained, treat the SVG portion as a consistency update that should follow the repository's diagram maintenance practice rather than as the primary justification for the commit.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was resolved persuasive/applied for R6 by Imaging Integration to add ImagingStudy.series.instance.numberOfFrames, with unsignedInt cardinality 0..1 and a DICOM mapping to Number Of Frames (0028,0008). That decision directly requires the active ImagingStudy conformance and reader-facing text to use the singular instance path and describe frame count rather than an instance ordinal.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a consistency check that flags when a newly added resource element is absent from the maintained resource diagram or when narrative mentions a non-existent element path.

source/measure/$care-gaps-request.txt                    | 2 +-
 source/measure/$care-gaps-request2.txt                   | 2 +-

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application, with mixed attribution: FHIR-56069 puts the active $care-gaps examples and explanatory text in scope, while FHIR-55967 is the specific decision that makes `reporter` the correct parameter instead of `organization`.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55967 explicitly removed the $care-gaps `organization` and `organizationResource` inputs and added `reporter` and `reporterResource`; the active request examples still used `organization=Organization/124`, so they conflicted with the current OperationDefinition parameter surface. FHIR-56069 separately resolved that the $care-gaps page examples and immediately following operation text should be updated because examples used removed or modified parameters, and the Measure introduction's change-note link naming FHIR-55069 was plainly inconsistent with that care-gaps issue. The update is required so the rendered operation page and included examples no longer advertise an input parameter that the current Jira-approved operation definition removed.

The OperationDefinition footer/comment text is rendered operation documentation and part of the conformance resource narrative, and the Measure introduction link is reader-visible provenance text.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix, but record the attribution as mixed: FHIR-56069 justifies revisiting the examples and page text, and FHIR-55967 justifies the `organization` to `reporter` parameter substitution.

jira_evidence.explanation: Resolved as Applied/Persuasive to update the $care-gaps operation page examples and explanatory text because many examples used parameters that had been removed or modified. This directly justifies correcting the active examples/page surface and the Measure introduction change-note attribution, although its pasted replacement text still used `organization` and therefore does not by itself identify the final valid parameter name.

FHIR-56069 alone is not a complete attribution for the parameter-name replacement because its resolution text still shows `organization`; FHIR-55967 supplies the concrete parameter decision.

This commit aligns the authoritative datatype guidance with the adopted type change.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-54848 was Applied/Persuasive with a Pharmacy vote to change Dosage.site to CodeableReference(BodyStructure) while keeping the existing CodeableConcept binding. After the structural change, source/datatypes/dosage.xml still had adjacent requirements/comment text saying the site was a coded specification and that BodyStructure-like detail should use the bodySite extension, which conflicts with the new CodeableReference capability. Because the datatype spreadsheet is the authoritative source for the rendered datatype element guidance and generated conformance narrative, updating those cells is required to complete the Jira decision rather than merely clean up source text.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/dosage.xml is the active Dosage datatype source; its element definition, requirements, and comments feed current rendered Dosage documentation and conformance-facing guidance. The stale text would mislead readers away from using the newly permitted BodyStructure reference for laterality/location qualifiers, while the proposed wording preserves the coded binding and describes the new referenced option.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed completion of FHIR-54848. Do not require a separate change for FHIR-54332 unless reviewers want an additional cross-reference, because the available evidence treats it as a duplicate of the same Dosage.site decision.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and its resolution specifically says to change dosage.site to CodeableReference(BodyStructure) while keeping the same binding on the CodeableConcept part. That directly requires nearby Dosage.site guidance to describe both coded and BodyStructure-reference usage instead of coded-only use plus extension guidance.

The cached materials do not include a Jira snapshot, but the cited Pharmacy minutes and reconciliation evidence describe it as the duplicate Dosage.site BodyStructure request closed in favor of FHIR-54848. It supports the duplicate context but is not needed for primary attribution.

caveats: The direct proof relies on the cached FHIR-54848 Jira snapshot and the source diff; no later conflicting decision was provided in the available evidence.
FHIR-54332 attribution is only supporting duplicate context here because its snapshot was not cached, but FHIR-54848 alone is sufficient to justify this narrow Dosage.site guidance change.

commits.summary: Completed the applied AdverseEvent.actuality unknown-code change by updating the build-scoped AdverseEvent-actuality SearchParameter description.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: Patient Care resolved to add an unknown value for AdverseEvent.actuality, while the active AdverseEvent actuality SearchParameter still described only actual and potential. Updating the description keeps the search parameter artifact aligned with the required-bound code set.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55315 was resolved as Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and specifically required adding an unknown code to the AdverseEvent.actuality code system and value set, with legacy-data semantics and discouraging guidance. The terminology and element metadata had been updated, but the AdverseEvent-actuality SearchParameter source still enumerated only actual and potential; because that SearchParameter describes token searches over AdverseEvent.actuality, the proposed update is required so the conformance artifact no longer omits a Jira-required allowed code.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the AdverseEvent SearchParameter bundle, which is authoritative source for current search parameter conformance/rendered content. The edit does not change the expression or validation behavior, but it corrects reader-facing and artifact-facing SearchParameter text so it no longer contradicts the value set and code system produced from the Jira decision.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a narrow Jira-backed completion of the AdverseEvent.actuality unknown-code change.

jira_evidence.explanation: Patient Care resolved the issue as Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6, requiring an unknown code for AdverseEvent.actuality with the definition that the source system does not specify which current value applies, plus a comment that the code is for legacy data and strongly discouraged. Once that code is present in the required-bound actuality value set, the SearchParameter description listing only actual and potential is stale and misleading.

caveats: Search parameter descriptions can legitimately differ from element descriptions, but this one is an explicit pipe-separated enumeration of actuality tokens; after FHIR-55315, omitting unknown incorrectly suggests the token is unavailable for search.

triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/datatypes/triggerdefinition.xml is authoritative datatype spreadsheet input, so its comments and invariant XPath affect generated conformance/rendered datatype content and validation support. source/eventdefinition/eventdefinition-notes.xml is rendered narrative for EventDefinition examples, so stale helper names and profile URLs are reader-visible and make the requested examples internally inconsistent.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution says to add the EventDefinition examples and, in addition, correct the invariants and guidance to clarify that condition is allowed on any trigger type, while only data-changed events populate the context and previous elements. After the Jira-linked removal, the authoritative FamilyMemberHistory.age[x] ElementDefinition still listed condition fhs-2 even though fhs-2 was the estimatedAge constraint and had been removed/commented out with the element. Removing that dangling condition is required to align the current conformance source with the WG decision.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition XML is authoritative conformance input, so a stale ElementDefinition.condition can affect generated ElementDefinition content and conformance/QA consistency. The FamilyMemberHistory SVG and library-fhir-model-definition files are generated or derived synchronization surfaces; they may affect checked-in rendered/packaged artifacts, but by themselves would be source hygiene rather than an independent spec-correctness basis.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the authoritative StructureDefinition change as the Jira-backed fix. Treat the SVG and model-info changes as regeneration/synchronization follow-through, and prefer regenerating or checking derived artifacts rather than relying on hand edits.

jira_evidence.explanation: Patient Care resolved the R6 core issue as Not Persuasive with Modification by removing FamilyMemberHistory.estimatedAge rather than expanding it to deceased[x]. That decision directly requires removing active conformance references to the estimatedAge-only fhs-2 invariant.

This related Patient Care no-change decision for estimate precision in an extension supports the clinical-actionability rationale cited in FHIR-54457, but it does not independently require the core FamilyMemberHistory edits.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Add or strengthen a consistency check so ElementDefinition.condition values cannot reference removed or commented-out constraints, and regenerate derived model-info and diagram artifacts from authoritative source.

commits.subject: FHIR-55448: Deduplicate DiagnosticReport conclusionCode summary flag
commits.summary: Removed a duplicate DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode isSummary flag left by overlapping summary-change implementations, while preserving the accepted FHIR-55448 summary end-state.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: the accepted DiagnosticReport summary decision requires conclusionCode to be a summary element, and the active StructureDefinition had two copies of the singleton summary flag. Keep the deduplication so the conformance source expresses the approved end state exactly once.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55448 resolved that DiagnosticReport.media should leave the summary and DiagnosticReport.conclusion and DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode should be added; the OO minutes confirm that result was not to be added merely because media had previously been included. The changed source surface is the active DiagnosticReport StructureDefinition, where conclusionCode already had the approved summary flag but had acquired a second duplicate isSummary entry from overlapping implementation history. Because ElementDefinition.isSummary is a single-valued conformance property, leaving two copies is not a correct expression of the Jira-approved end state; removing the duplicate preserves the approved summary semantics while making the authoritative source well-formed for generated conformance output.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The edited XML is the authoritative DiagnosticReport StructureDefinition input, so its ElementDefinition flags feed the rendered element tables, generated StructureDefinition artifacts, summary views, validation metadata, and QA. The change does not alter the WG-approved semantic choice that conclusionCode is in the summary; it removes invalid duplicate singleton content from the current conformance source.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed source correction. No WG re-vote is needed for the deduplication, but related summary-change history can be audited under FHIR-54554 if reviewers want to confirm both overlapping implementations landed cleanly.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 DiagnosticReport and resolved to remove .media from the summary while adding .conclusion and .conclusionCode. That establishes the current approved summary end state that the active StructureDefinition must represent, with conclusionCode summarized once rather than duplicated.

This earlier Applied/Persuasive with Modification issue resolved to add both DiagnosticReport.conclusion and DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode as summary elements. Its overlapping implementation explains how conclusionCode ended up with a duplicate summary flag, but it does not require any different semantic outcome from FHIR-55448.

triage.tooling_recommendation: A QA check for duplicate singleton ElementDefinition children, especially isSummary, would catch this class of overlapping-implementation error earlier.
caveats: The semantic summary decision was already present before this commit; the remaining problem was duplicate singleton conformance content in the active source.
The related FHIR-54554 history is useful context for why the duplicate occurred, but FHIR-55448 itself is sufficient attribution for the required DiagnosticReport summary end state.

The Provenance introduction had already been updated through the Jira-linked implementation to say Activity acts upon output (.target) resources, but source/provenance/structuredefinition-Provenance.xml still used the old ElementDefinition text. Because that StructureDefinition is the authoritative source for the current Provenance conformance artifact and rendered element definition, the proposed wording change is required to align the built spec with the Jira decision; the mapping-exception source is a companion consistency update for the same element definition text.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition change affects current rendered Provenance.activity definition text and the generated conformance artifact. Leaving the old wording would continue to imply that read/query or validation-only processing can be a Provenance activity, contrary to the accepted clarification. The mapping-exception file reflects the same source definition alignment; the unrelated newline normalization in a comment has no substantive spec impact.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed Provenance clarification. If reviewing narrowly, focus approval on the Provenance.activity ElementDefinition and its matching mapping-exception text; no new Jira or WG path is needed for this wording alignment.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Provenance and explicitly objected to wording that an activity may include consuming or processing entities, explaining that Provenance does not track query/read or validation-only actions and that consumed or processed entities matter only when involved in creating a target. That resolution directly supports replacing the stale Provenance.activity definition with the output-target wording already applied to the Provenance introduction.

caveats: The evidence for current spec impact rests on source/provenance/structuredefinition-Provenance.xml as the active Provenance StructureDefinition input; source/provenance/provenance-event-mapping-exceptions.xml is treated as a related consistency surface rather than the primary conformance source.

commits.summary: Updated stale Composition invariant fixtures so relatesTo.type uses CodeableConcept codings instead of the pre-FHIR-52968 primitive code representation.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-52968 changed Composition.relatesTo.type to CodeableConcept with an extensible THO artifact-relationship binding, but the Composition invariant-test fixtures still used the prior primitive code serialization. Updating those fixtures keeps the current invariant QA examples aligned with the approved R6 datatype.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-52968 specifically resolved that Composition.relatesTo.type must change from code with required binding to CodeableConcept with extensible binding to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/artifact-relationship-type. The current StructureDefinition already reflects that decision, but the cmp-* invariant fixtures under source/composition/invariant-tests still serialized relatesTo.type as <type value="replaces"/> and <type value="appends"/>, which conflicts with the approved element shape. Because these files are invariant-test fixtures for the current Composition constraints, leaving an unrelated datatype error in them can make pass/fail fixtures validate for the wrong reason; wrapping the same relationship codes in CodeableConcept.coding is the required alignment with the Jira decision.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed files are not normative narrative pages or generated summaries, but they are current source test fixtures for Composition invariants. Their correctness affects QA/validation of the current Composition conformance rules: stale primitive relatesTo.type values are invalid against the approved R6 StructureDefinition and can obscure whether cmp-1, cmp-2, or cmp-3 themselves are being tested correctly.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fixture correction. No new WG path is needed for these files because the datatype decision was already made in FHIR-52968; reviewers should only confirm the fixture harness expects otherwise-valid resources apart from the targeted invariant failure.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive R6 resolution explicitly requires Composition.relatesTo.type to be CodeableConcept and to use an extensible binding to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/artifact-relationship-type. The fixture update applies that exact datatype and terminology shape to current Composition invariant-test resources.

FHIR-52920 explains the cmp-3 invariant context and why some of the affected Composition invariant fixtures exist, but it does not justify the relatesTo.type datatype change. The datatype attribution remains FHIR-52968.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider making invariant-test fixture validation report unrelated datatype errors distinctly from expected invariant pass/fail results so stale fixture shapes cannot silently mask the constraint being tested.
caveats: The authoritative Composition StructureDefinition was already correct; this commit is limited to QA fixture alignment.
FHIR-52920 is background only and should not be cited as the responsible decision for the relatesTo.type representation.

The current ValueSet $validate-code OperationDefinition source already had system-version and check-system-version but omitted force-system-version, so it remained out of alignment with the decided parameter set. caveats: This triage relies on the cached FHIR-52907 snapshot for the final decision; additional cited broader cleanup tickets are unresolved and do not change the required parameter addition.
The change is limited to the authoritative OperationDefinition XML and does not include generated-only artifacts.

commits.subject: FHIR-38957: Clarify CodeableReference constraint mapping
commits.summary: Clarified the active CodeableReference narrative so targetProfile and binding constraints declared on CodeableReference map to reference and concept respectively.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application. FHIR-38957 explicitly approved replacing the CodeableReference constraint sentence with wording that maps targetProfile to reference and binding to concept, and this commit aligns the active datatype narrative with that decision.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-38957 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification with concrete replacement text: targetProfile and binding constraints declared on CodeableReference apply to CodeableReference.reference and CodeableReference.concept respectively, and must not be specified directly on the child elements. The current source/references.html wording still said the constraints apply to reference or concept "respectively as appropriate", preserving the ambiguity the Jira was meant to remove. Because this paragraph is the active CodeableReference datatype narrative, the proposed wording is required to bring the rendered guidance into alignment with the approved resolution.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/references.html is reader-visible datatype narrative for CodeableReference. The change does not alter conformance artifacts directly, but it corrects current rendered explanatory text so it matches the StructureDefinition sdf-24 and sdf-25 constraints that require targetProfile and binding to be declared on CodeableReference rather than on CodeableReference.reference or CodeableReference.concept.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed clarification in the active references narrative. The attribution to FHIR-38957 is direct; FHIR-39176 supports retaining the SHALL NOT wording, and FHIR-39132 is related context for the same paragraph.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically approved replacing the confusing CodeableReference constraint wording with the one-to-one mapping used by this commit: targetProfile constraints apply to CodeableReference.reference, binding constraints apply to CodeableReference.concept, and those constraints SHALL NOT be specified directly on the child elements.

This related Published issue resolved that the same paragraph must use SHALL NOT, because sdf-24 and sdf-25 are error-level StructureDefinition constraints. It supports preserving the prohibition in the updated wording.

This related Published issue addressed neighboring ambiguity in the same CodeableReference paragraph. It does not drive the exact mapping change, but confirms the paragraph was an approved clarification surface.

caveats: The changed file is narrative HTML rather than an authoritative StructureDefinition, so the direct impact is rendered reader guidance, not generated constraint behavior.
The commit leaves the existing commented-out sentence untouched; the active rendered sentence is the relevant source surface for this triage.

commits.subject: FHIR-55366: Remove MeasureReport non-modifier metadata
commits.summary: Removed the remaining modifier metadata and stale modifier prose from the active MeasureReport elements covered by FHIR-55366.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application for MeasureReport modifier metadata. FHIR-55366 specifically directed removing Is Modifier and the modifier reason from scoring, dataUpdateType, and improvementNotation, and this change removes the leftover metadata and obsolete modifier prose from the active MeasureReport StructureDefinition source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-55366 resolved that MeasureReport scoring, dataUpdateType, and improvementNotation do not meet the definition of Is Modifier and that both the Is Modifier flag and modifier reason should be removed for all three elements. The current StructureDefinition source had only partially reflected that decision: the elements had been changed to non-modifier but still carried explicit non-modifier entries, modifier reasons, and an improvementNotation comment saying the element was labeled as a modifier. Because this StructureDefinition is the authoritative MeasureReport conformance source, those leftovers conflict with the resolved element metadata and rendered element prose. The proposed update is required to finish aligning the active source with the CQI resolution while preserving the separate Measure-to-MeasureReport interpretation guidance.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative MeasureReport StructureDefinition XML, so its element metadata and comments flow into current conformance artifacts and rendered element documentation. Leaving modifier reasons and prose that says improvementNotation is labeled as a modifier would continue to publish stale conformance-facing and reader-visible information after the Jira decision removed that status.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as the direct Jira-backed completion of FHIR-55366. No separate WG path is needed for the removed modifier metadata or the targeted comment cleanup.

jira_evidence.explanation: The applied CQI resolution agreed that scoring, dataUpdateType, and improvementNotation do not meet the definition for Is Modifier and explicitly said to remove Is Modifier and the reason for all three elements. That directly requires removing the leftover modifier metadata and obsolete modifier-label sentence from the MeasureReport source.

This related applied clarification added Measure-to-MeasureReport population guidance that appears in the same improvementNotation comment. It supports preserving that guidance while removing only the obsolete modifier assertion, but it does not itself justify the modifier metadata removal.

This later Measure/MeasureReport approach decision explains why the current relevant scoring and improvementNotation targets are group-level MeasureReport elements rather than removed or deprecated root-level calculation elements. It supports the source location selection but is not the direct basis for removing modifier metadata.

caveats: The triage depends on the StructureDefinition XML being the authoritative conformance source for MeasureReport; this is not a generated-only or example-only cleanup.
The change intentionally preserves substantive interpretation guidance added by related MeasureReport clarifications and removes only the stale modifier claim and modifier-reason metadata.

The commit completes that alignment in the authoritative PaymentReconciliation StructureDefinition and updates the example to remain valid with the changed datatype.

triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition change affects current conformance content, rendered element tables, validation expectations, and generated artifacts for PaymentReconciliation. Changing processNote.type from code to CodeableConcept with extensible note-type binding, requiring text, adding language, and aligning the explicit type name all change the normative resource model exposed by the current build; the example update follows from that model change so the checked-in example remains valid.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix completing the Applied FM decision; regenerate any derived diagrams or generated summaries through the normal build rather than hand-editing them.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue is Applied/Persuasive for R6 and says to match the structure of processNote in PaymentReconciliation to ClaimResponse and add a 0..* allocation note reference. That resolution directly requires PaymentReconciliation.processNote to use the same current ClaimResponse child structure, including the Note backbone name, CodeableConcept note type with extensible binding, required text, and language child.

This related FM decision is reported to have changed the ClaimResponse and ExplanationOfBenefit processNote.type shape to CodeableConcept with an extensible note-type binding. It helps explain the ClaimResponse target that FHIR-53200 tells PaymentReconciliation to match, but the direct authority for editing PaymentReconciliation here is FHIR-53200.

This related FM decision is reported to have added processNote.class to ClaimResponse and ExplanationOfBenefit. It supports the history of the ClaimResponse processNote shape, while FHIR-53200 supplies the direct PaymentReconciliation alignment decision.

This related decision is reported to be part of the ClaimResponse processNote.text history. It supports why the current ClaimResponse target has markdown note text, but does not replace FHIR-53200 as the direct PaymentReconciliation basis.

This related decision is reported to be part of the PaymentReconciliation processNote.text history. It supports the processNote-family context, but the decisive requirement to match ClaimResponse comes from FHIR-53200.

caveats: The cached snapshot for FHIR-53200 is sufficient for attribution because it explicitly names both the PaymentReconciliation source surface and the ClaimResponse comparison target.
The supporting related-Jira details were not independently cached here; they are useful context for the ClaimResponse target shape, not necessary to justify this commit.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution requires renderedInstruction to be mandatory and to communicate the full dosage intent, including a SHALL statement that renderedInstructions contain the structured dosage information. This related patient-instruction placement topic was only cited as background and does not provide the applied decision for the narrative change.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-53412: Clarify Timing offset source text
commits.summary: Applied FHIR-53412 was already substantially present, but the current source still had seed-scope wording and markup defects around the new Timing offsets. The reconciliation corrected those defects without taking over later unresolved offset redesign work.
commits.stat:
source/datatypes.html       | 2 +-
 source/datatypes/timing.xml | 4 ++--
 source/dosage-examples.html | 2 +-
 3 files changed, 4 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-53412 decided that Timing.repeat.startOffset and Timing.repeat.endOffset are core Timing elements and that the Timing repeat-window behavior should be clarified. This commit fixes bounded source text defects left by that application in active datatype and example source.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-53412 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and specifically resolved to add Timing.repeat.startOffset and Timing.repeat.endOffset, while clarifying how Timing.repeat.when relates to the implicit repeat window and dropping the proposed event elements. The current source already had those additions, but active source still contradicted or damaged that decision: the endOffset row used the nonsensical verb "step" where the resolved behavior is that repeat-period events stop before the end of the period, the new Timing narrative had a malformed code tag around count, and a dosage example still described startOffset as an extension rather than the newly added core element. Updating those strings is required to make the source application match the Jira decision rather than leaving reader-visible and conformance-facing residue from an incomplete application.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The edited Timing spreadsheet source is authoritative for generated datatype definitions, source/datatypes.html contributes rendered datatype narrative, and source/dosage-examples.html is reader-visible example guidance. The changes therefore affect current rendered/conformance-facing text rather than only repository hygiene or generated-only synchronization.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed cleanup for FHIR-53412, limited to the wording and markup defects shown here. Broader Timing offset constraints, example-table changes, or dosage-cycle modeling should remain on their own applied Jira path.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue was Applied/Persuasive with a 2025-11-10 FHIR-I vote to add Timing.repeat.startOffset and Timing.repeat.endOffset and add clarifying text about the repeat window, while not adding startEvent/endEvent. That decision directly requires active Timing and Dosage text not to present startOffset as an extension, not to leave malformed markup in the new clarification, and not to describe endOffset with wording inconsistent with a repeat period stopping before its end.

caveats: The Jira resolution text itself appears to carry the original "step" typo in the endOffset definition, but the same resolution's comments and the requested repeat-window behavior describe schedules that stop before the period end; this commit corrects that implementation typo without taking on later unresolved offset redesign work.

Related later issues such as FHIR-54058, FHIR-54062, and FHIR-54252 may require broader Timing example, constraint, or dosage modeling work, but they are not needed to justify these bounded source-text fixes.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-41456: Correct Consent provision-code search parameter
commits.summary: Completed the applied Consent.provision.code search-parameter change by correcting the copied Consent-action URL and code.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-41456 resolved to add a Consent search parameter for provision.code, but the checked-in Consent search-parameter bundle still identified that new entry with the Consent-action canonical URL and action code. Correcting the URL and code is required so the current generated SearchParameter metadata exposes the intended provision-code parameter rather than a duplicated/misleading action parameter.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-41456 was Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core Consent and specifically resolved to add a search parameter supporting searches on Consent.provision.code. The implementation added an entry with id Consent-provision-code, path Consent.provision.code, and expression Consent.repeat(provision).code, but left copied identifiers from Consent-action in the SearchParameter.url and SearchParameter.code fields. Because those identifiers define the published search parameter canonical and client-facing search code, the source remained out of alignment with the Jira decision until they were changed to Consent-provision-code and provision-code.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/consent/bundle-Consent-search-params.xml is authoritative source for Consent search parameters in the current build. The stale URL/code would affect rendered/generated SearchParameter conformance metadata and could make the provision-code expression appear as another action parameter instead of the new search parameter requested by the Jira.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-41456. FHIR-50868 should not be treated as the basis for this identifier correction; it is only later background on the resulting Consent.action/provision-code QA symptom.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue is Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core Consent and its resolution says to add a search parameter for provision.code. That decision requires a distinct SearchParameter whose canonical URL and code identify provision-code, not action.

The later Consent QA issue made Consent search parameters active/normative and called out Consent-provision-code in the QA context, but it did not itself decide the provision-code URL/code naming. It confirms the affected entry is current conformance source rather than historical residue.

The later issue reported a QA message where Consent.action had expression Consent.provision.code, but its resolution was to add Consent.action to examples. It is useful evidence of the bad copied identifier state, not the responsible decision for this source correction.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Consider a publisher/QA check that flags SearchParameter entries whose id, url tail, code, path, and expression indicate conflicting parameters, especially when a bundle contains duplicate canonical URLs or duplicate codes with different expressions.
caveats: This assessment is limited to the URL/code correction in the Consent search-parameter bundle; it does not endorse unrelated example changes suggested by later QA discussion.

The original FHIR-41456 implementation commit added Consent-provision-code with copied Consent-action URL/code values, so the defect appears to be an incomplete application of that Jira rather than a later intentional rename.

jira_evidence.explanation: The issue identified NutritionProduct.status as mandatory with a required binding and no unknown or other escape-valve concept. commits.summary: Completed the applied Medication serial-number change by aligning the remaining active search-parameter, definition-comment, and contained-example surfaces with Medication.instance.identifier.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-47622 explicitly moved Medication physical-instance identifiers from the general Medication.identifier space into Medication.instance.identifier. The commit aligns the remaining authoritative Medication definition and search-parameter inputs with that decision, while also updating stale contained Medication examples from the removed batch element to instance.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-47622 was applied as a persuasive R6 Pharmacy decision to rename Medication.batch to Medication.instance, add Medication.instance.identifier 0..* Identifier for the physical instance, typically a serial number, and ensure serial numbers are not carried in Medication.identifier examples. The remaining source still had a Medication.identifier comment allowing serial numbers there, a serial-number SearchParameter expression pointing at Medication.identifier, a stale lot-number path using Medication.batch, and active contained Medication examples using the old batch element. The proposed update is required to make those current source surfaces reflect the renamed backbone element and the dedicated serial-number location decided by the Jira.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml and source/medication/bundle-Medication-search-params.xml are authoritative conformance/search-parameter inputs, so stale comments, path extensions, and expressions would affect rendered conformance content and search behavior. The example edits keep current example source aligned with the renamed Medication backbone element; even if some example cleanup would be less critical by itself, the commit as a whole corrects authoritative current spec inputs.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-47622. If reviewing similar follow-up commits, prioritize the StructureDefinition and SearchParameter corrections as required, and treat the example renames as appropriate consistency cleanup tied to the same element rename.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically says to rename the current Medication batch BackboneElement to instance, add identifier 0..* Identifier to that backbone element for the physical instance, typically a serial number, and make sure existing examples do not carry serial numbers in Medication.identifier. That directly supports redirecting Medication.identifier commentary and the serial-number SearchParameter to Medication.instance.identifier, changing lot-number paths from Medication.batch to Medication.instance, and replacing stale batch elements in current Medication examples.

caveats: The search-parameter description wording is not being justified by equality with an element definition; it is justified because the previous serial-number entry described and queried the wrong concept and expression after FHIR-47622.

The contained example changes alone might warrant checking whether the publisher strips unknown elements, but the same commit also fixes authoritative StructureDefinition and SearchParameter inputs, so the overall source change is not merely repository hygiene.

commits.subject: FHIR-50539: Align DetectedIssue expectedOnsetType binding
commits.summary: Aligned DetectedIssue.expectedOnsetType with the Applied FHIR-50539 resolution by changing its binding to extensible and restoring the rapid-onset pending-code note in rendered value-set content.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-50539 explicitly required DetectedIssue.expectedOnsetType to use an extensible binding and to carry a value-set note that a rapid-onset concept has been requested. The current DetectedIssue StructureDefinition and value set still showed an example binding and omitted that reader-visible note.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-50539 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and its resolution required DetectedIssue.expectedOnsetType as 0..1 CodeableConcept, with rapid/delayed onset semantics, an extensible binding to the expected-onset value set, SNOMED CT sudden/delayed concepts, and a note that a rapid-onset concept has been requested. The current authoritative DetectedIssue StructureDefinition retained example binding strength and example-oriented binding text, while the active value-set description did not contain the requested rapid-code note. Updating the binding strength/description and restoring the note in rendered value-set content is required to align the active source with the approved resolution.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The StructureDefinition XML is an authoritative conformance input, so the binding strength affects generated conformance artifacts, rendered element tables, and validation expectations for DetectedIssue.expectedOnsetType. The ValueSet XML description is active terminology source and reader-visible rendered content, so omitting the rapid-onset pending-code note loses part of the approved terminology guidance.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep this as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-50539. Treat any future move of the value set to THO as a separate terminology migration decision rather than part of this correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: The Applied/Persuasive resolution specifically says to add DetectedIssue.expectedOnsetType as 0..1 CodeableConcept, bound extensible to a value set including the available SNOMED CT delayed and sudden concepts, and to note in the value set that a rapid-onset concept has been requested and should be included once available. That directly requires the binding-strength and value-set-description updates in this commit.

A later DetectedIssue terminology migration issue was noted as background, but it is not needed to justify this commit and does not supersede the FHIR-50539 binding-strength and rapid-code-note correction.

caveats: This triage only supports the current core value set and binding correction; it does not justify changing the canonical to terminology.hl7.org without a final THO migration decision.
The value-set note is part of the Jira resolution, not merely source cleanup, because moving it into the ValueSet description makes it survive as rendered terminology guidance.

commits.subject: FHIR-50484: Correct Measure evaluate examples
commits.summary: Corrected the current Measure/$evaluate request examples so they match the DEQM-aligned type-level operation shape.

triage.reviewer_summary: This is a Jira-backed missed application: the Measure/$evaluate request examples still showed instance-level invocation after the applied DEQM-alignment decision made the operation type-level only with required measureUrl. The proposed edit brings the rendered examples back into alignment with the current OperationDefinition.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-50484 was applied with a resolution to align base FHIR Measure/$evaluate with the DEQM operation, review and update the operation examples, and correct the old example URLs to $evaluate. A later comment on that same issue explicitly imported the DEQM simplification from FHIR-51856: remove the old measure/url/version selectors, replace them with measureUrl 1..*, and remove instance-level invocation. The current OperationDefinition already reflects that decision with type=true, instance=false, and measureUrl 1..*, but source/measure/$evaluate-request.txt still invoked [base]/Measure/CMS146/$evaluate without measureUrl and had the patient-specific example using an untyped subject plus a periodEnd casing typo. Because that request file is attached through the OperationDefinition example extension, the stale text is a current rendered operation example, not just source-tree residue. Updating the URLs to [base]/Measure/$evaluate with measureUrl is required to complete the applied Jira decision.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file affects the current rendered Measure/$evaluate operation examples. It does not alter the authoritative OperationDefinition parameters, but without this edit the published request examples contradict the current conformance definition by demonstrating an instance-level call and omitting the required measureUrl parameter.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as a Jira-backed fix for FHIR-50484. Treat related Measure/$evaluate parameter and return-documentation issues separately; this commit is narrowly about correcting the current request examples.

jira_evidence.explanation: The applied resolution required aligning base FHIR Measure/$evaluate with DEQM, reviewing and updating the examples on the operation page, and correcting old example URLs to $evaluate. Its comments also state that the base FHIR alignment must include the DEQM simplification that removes instance-level invocation and uses required measureUrl.

This DEQM change is cited from FHIR-50484 as the target simplification: remove measure/url/version selector parameters, replace them with measureUrl 1..*, and remove the ability to invoke the operation at the Measure instance level. It supports the exact request-example shape used by this commit, but the base FHIR authority for applying it here is FHIR-50484.

triage.tooling_recommendation: none
caveats: The change is limited to rendered request examples; the OperationDefinition itself already had the aligned type-level invocation and measureUrl cardinality.
FHIR-50488, FHIR-50489, and FHIR-51487 concern other Measure/$evaluate details and do not need to be bundled with this example correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution specifically required intervalUnit to cover "interval or offsets" and required a constraint that one of interval or offsets, but not both, be present. The changed spreadsheet cells directly correct stale source wording that conflicted with those requirements.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-51587: Complete SearchParameter FHIRPath guidance
commits.summary: Completed the applied FHIR-I guidance for SearchParameter FHIRPath expressions and corrected invalid FHIRPath examples in the same guidance.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application. FHIR-51587's final FHIR-I disposition explicitly required SearchParameter FHIRPath guidance in both the notes page and the SearchParameter.expression element comment; the current source had the notes but not the element comment and still showed invalid FHIRPath examples.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-51587 was resolved as a clarification requiring guidance that SearchParameter.expression permits full FHIRPath but warns against resolve() traversing across resource instance boundaries, with chaining as the intended cross-boundary search mechanism. The active SearchParameter StructureDefinition still omitted that approved guidance from the SearchParameter.expression comment, while the SearchParameter notes contained examples using the invalid descendent/descendents spelling. Adding the approved comment and correcting the visible FHIRPath examples brings the current SearchParameter source into alignment with the work-group decision.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The SearchParameter StructureDefinition is an authoritative conformance input, so its element comment affects rendered element documentation and generated conformance content. The SearchParameter notes file is reader-visible narrative; publishing invalid FHIRPath in a section about FHIRPath expression guidance would undermine current specification correctness.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed fix. Do not reintroduce the earlier simple-subset restriction; future validation policy or enforceable FHIRPath profiles should come through ballot feedback or a separate work-group decision.

jira_evidence.explanation: The final Applied/Persuasive with Modification resolution required a new SearchParameter notes section, the same resolve()/resource-boundary guidance as an additional comment on SearchParameter.expression, and a ballot note. This commit supplies the missing element comment and fixes invalid FHIRPath examples in the already-added notes guidance.

FHIR-49784 required use of repeat() in search parameter expressions for nested elements, which conflicted with the earlier simple-subset approach for FHIR-51587. FHIR-I reopened FHIR-51587 and chose guidance rather than a restrictive subset, supporting the wording used here but not independently requiring this edit.

triage.tooling_recommendation: Add or maintain validation for FHIRPath snippets in SearchParameter narrative guidance, not only formal SearchParameter.expression values, so misspelled functions such as descendants() are caught before publication.
caveats: The notes typo correction is not a separately quoted Jira resolution item, but it is in active reader-visible guidance introduced for the FHIRPath validation issue and prevents publishing invalid FHIRPath in that section.
FHIR-51580 is background for removing concrete cross-resource resolve() search expressions, not needed to justify this commit.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-47677: Fix Appointment is-recurring search expression
commits.summary: Corrected the Appointment is-recurring search parameter so it uses logical OR for the approved recurrence-template-or-originating-appointment semantics.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-47677 explicitly approved an Appointment is-recurring token search parameter that is true when the Appointment has a recurrence template or an originating appointment. The current SearchParameter expression used the FHIRPath union operator between booleans, so changing it to logical `or` is required to match the approved semantics.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-47677 was resolved Applied/Persuasive with Modification and specifically required five Appointment recurrence-series search parameters, including is-recurring as a token with "has template OR has originating appointment" semantics. The active Appointment search-parameter bundle already contains the requested parameter, but its expression used `Appointment.recurrenceTemplate.exists() | Appointment.originatingAppointment.exists()`, which is a union expression rather than the Jira-approved boolean disjunction. Updating the expression to `Appointment.recurrenceTemplate.exists() or Appointment.originatingAppointment.exists()` is the direct source change needed to align the generated SearchParameter with the responsible Jira decision.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is the authoritative Appointment search-parameter source, so its expression affects the generated SearchParameter conformance artifact and the normative search behavior described by the current specification. This is not merely source cleanup; the old expression encoded the approved recurrence-series search semantics incorrectly.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep the change as the Jira-backed fix for FHIR-47677. No additional Jira attribution or WG path appears necessary for this narrow expression correction.

jira_evidence.explanation: The resolution expressly approved Appointment recurrence search support and listed is-recurring as a token search parameter with "has template OR has originating appointment" semantics; that directly requires a boolean OR expression over recurrenceTemplate.exists() and originatingAppointment.exists().

caveats: This assessment depends on the active Appointment search-parameter bundle as the current source of the generated SearchParameter artifact.

commits.author: Josh Mandel
commits.subject: FHIR-51607: Link published compartment extension
commits.summary: Removed stale unpublished-extension wording from the active StructureDefinition additional-resource narrative and linked to the published additional-resource-compartment extension.

triage.reviewer_summary: Jira-backed missed application: FHIR-51607 accepted an additional-resource-compartment extension mechanism for documenting compartment membership of additional resources, and the active StructureDefinition narrative still described that extension as not yet published. The commit removes that stale publication caveat and links the published canonical extension.
triage.category_rationale: FHIR-51607 resolved to define a repeatable additionalResourceCompartment extension on StructureDefinition for additional resources, including components for the compartment, membership search parameters, documentation, and $everything start/end parameters. The current StructureDefinition additional-resource rules already point to that mechanism but still say the extension is "yet to be published"; because the extension is now published and the line is active resource narrative, retaining that caveat leaves the specification text out of alignment with the accepted resolution and current extension registry state. Updating the sentence to link the published additional-resource-compartment extension is required to complete the Jira-backed documentation path without implying the mechanism is still future work.
triage.fhir_spec_impact: The changed file is active StructureDefinition narrative source, so this affects current rendered explanatory text for additional-resource StructureDefinitions. It does not change conformance cardinalities or CompartmentDefinition instances, but it corrects reader-visible guidance and the canonical reference used to understand how post-R6 additional resources document compartment membership.
triage.recommended_reviewer_action: Keep as a Jira-backed narrative correction for FHIR-51607. Do not expand this into CompartmentDefinition instance edits; detailed extension-definition refinements, if any, belong in the extension/tooling source that publishes the additional-resource-compartment extension.

jira_evidence.explanation: The applied resolution specifically required defining an additionalResourceCompartment extension on StructureDefinition to document compartment membership determinations for additional resources, with compartment, param, documentation, startParam, and endParam components. The edited narrative is the core documentation surface for those additional-resource rules and was still describing the accepted extension as unpublished.

This issue clarified that HL7-defined CompartmentDefinition instances are not a computable mechanism for a server's additional or reduced compartment implementation. That supports using the StructureDefinition extension mechanism rather than changing current core CompartmentDefinition instances.

caveats: The proof depends on the extension having been published after the original core wording was added; the Jira resolution itself established the extension mechanism, while the publication state makes the old qualifier stale.
FHIR-50848 may provide same-family context for the extension mechanism, but the cached evidence for this triage is sufficient to attribute this specific core narrative correction to FHIR-51607.
